beats.text: Number three: Trump's trip to Ireland orbited one thing — the Irish Open at his own Doonbeg resort.

beats.caption: I built it about 22 years, right on the ocean.
beats.label: via The White House

beats.text: He didn't build it. Trump bought the resort around 2014 — the course was designed by Greg Norman and opened back in 2002.

beats.caption: He's having a good time. Great course. Nice hotel.
beats.label: via The White House

beats.text: Rory McIlroy, who actually plays the place, was asked how he felt about Trump's visit.

beats.caption: That brings more attention and eyeballs to the Irish Open, and I think that can only be a good thing.
beats.label: via The FOREcast Golf

beats.text: Diplomatic. Almost as diplomatic as Trump grading his own weekend, on the way out of the country.

beats.caption: The tournament was record setting. The attendance was number one.
beats.label: via The White House
